\subsection*{Randomized --- RPExpected: Results}

\begin{definition}[Randomized exponential-time decision predicate]
\lean{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInExpTime}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p021-b005,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p021-b006
}
\label{Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInExpTime}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.randProb, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.ExpTimeLe, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith}
Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let
$L$ be a language of Boolean strings, and let $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. For
every Boolean string $x$, the machine's runtime is at most $T(|x|)$. If $x\in L$, then
for every rational $\varepsilon>0$ there is a number of random choice bits $t$ for which
the probability that the machine halts with output `[true]` is at least
$2/3-\varepsilon$. If $x\notin L$, then every choice-bit string $w$ whose run halts
produces output `[false]`.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Randomized exponential-time class]
\lean{Randomized.RP_ExpPTM}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p021-b005,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p021-b006
}
\label{Randomized.RP_ExpPTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.FinNDTM.RDecidesInExpTime}
The class consists of all languages $L$ of Boolean strings for which there are natural
numbers $c,e$ and a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the Boolean
alphabet satisfying the following conditions: on every input $x$, its runtime is at most
$c(|x|^e+1)$; on inputs in $L$, its acceptance probability can be made at least
$2/3-\varepsilon$ for every rational $\varepsilon>0$ by choosing a suitable number of
random choice bits; and on inputs outside $L$, every halted run outputs `[false]`.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Complement of the randomized exponential-time class]
\lean{Randomized.coRP_ExpPTM}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p022-b003}
\label{Randomized.coRP_ExpPTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RP_ExpPTM}
The class of languages $L$ over Boolean strings whose complement belongs to
$\mathrm{RP\_ExpPTM}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Constant acceptance probability amplification]
\lean{Randomized.InRPWith.inRP_of_const}
\label{Randomized.InRPWith.inRP_of_const}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.InRP, Randomized.InRPWith, Randomized.anyVerifier, Randomized.blockCount, Randomized.exists_ofFn_eq, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.polyTimeModel_closedUnderAny, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_blockCount, Randomized.randProb_congr, Randomized.randProb_le_one, Randomized.randProb_not}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\rho$ be a rational number, let $K$ be a natural number, and suppose $(1-\rho)^K\le
1/3$. For any language $L$ of bit strings, if an efficient verifier with a polynomial
random-bit bound accepts every member with probability at least $\rho$ and rejects every
nonmember for every choice of random bits, then $L$ has an efficient verifier with a
polynomial random-bit bound that accepts every member with probability at least $2/3$
and rejects every nonmember for every choice of random bits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected-time randomized recognition implies RP]
\lean{Randomized.inRP_of_mem_RP_ExpPTM}
\label{Randomized.inRP_of_mem_RP_ExpPTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.exists_choiceVerifier_mem_P, Randomized.InRP, Randomized.InRPWith.inRP_of_const, Randomized.RP_ExpPTM, Randomized.eff_append_mem, Randomized.indicator_eq_true_iff, Randomized.polyLen, Randomized.polyTimeModel, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_mono, Turing.FinNDTM.haltProb_le_truncate, Turing.FinNDTM.haltProb_mono, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.choiceBudget_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let $L$ be a language of bit strings in the class of languages recognized by a finite
nondeterministic Turing machine with a polynomial expected-time bound, where random
choice bits select its transitions. On members, for every $\varepsilon>0$ some number of
random bits gives probability at least $2/3-\varepsilon$ of halting with output true; on
nonmembers, every halting run outputs false. Then $L$ has an efficient one-sided
randomized verifier in the polynomial-time verifier model: it accepts members with
probability at least $2/3$ and rejects nonmembers with certainty.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-Time Randomized Computation Is Included in Expected-Time Randomized Computation]
\lean{Randomized.RP_PTM_subset_RP_ExpPTM}
\label{Randomized.RP_PTM_subset_RP_ExpPTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RP_ExpPTM, Randomized.RP_PTM, Randomized.randProb, Randomized.randProb_congr, Turing.FinNDTM.expTimeLe_of_haltsWithin, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_eq_some_iff, Turing.FinNDTM.haltRun_isPrefixStable, Turing.FinNDTM.outputProb, Turing.FinNDTM.outputWith, Turing.FinNDTM.runWith_eq_runWith_take}
\difficulty{5}
Every language decidable in polynomial time by a randomized machine with one-sided error
and acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on members belongs to the class defined by a
polynomial bound on cumulative probabilities of not yet halting, acceptance probability
arbitrarily close to at least $2/3$ on members, and no accepting output on any halted
branch for nonmembers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of Two Randomized Polynomial-Time Classes]
\lean{Randomized.RP_ExpPTM_eq_RP_PTM}
\label{Randomized.RP_ExpPTM_eq_RP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RP_ExpPTM, Randomized.RP_PTM, Randomized.RP_PTM_subset_RP_ExpPTM, Randomized.inRP_of_mem_RP_ExpPTM, Randomized.mem_RP_PTM_iff}
\difficulty{1}
The class of languages decidable by a randomized Turing machine with a polynomial bound
on the cumulative probabilities of not yet having halted, acceptance probability
arbitrarily close to at least $2/3$ on members, and no accepting output on any halted
branch for nonmembers, equals the class of languages decidable in polynomial time with
one-sided error: members are accepted with probability at least $2/3$, and nonmembers
are never accepted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of coRP classes]
\lean{Randomized.coRP_ExpPTM_eq_coRP_PTM}
\label{Randomized.coRP_ExpPTM_eq_coRP_PTM}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RP_ExpPTM, Randomized.RP_ExpPTM_eq_RP_PTM, Randomized.RP_PTM, Randomized.coRP_ExpPTM, Randomized.coRP_PTM}
\difficulty{1}
The class of complements of languages in RP with expected polynomial time equals the
class of complements of languages in RP with polynomial worst-case time.
\end{theorem}
